newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer, await 10-year bond auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer, await 10-year bond auction.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher on Tuesday, supported by weaker Tokyo share prices, traders said.
Trade was thin, with investors sidelined ahead of a 10-year JGB auction due on Wednesday, they said. Traders said the coupon rate for the new 10-year issue is likely to be set at 2.5 percent.
Market players said they were are also focusing on testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan at 1800 GMT.

"If U.S. share prices fall as a result of Greenspan's comments on the economy, the impact may spill over into the Tokyo stock market and have an indirect effect on the (Tokyo) bond market," said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
The September ended at 125.13, up slightly from Friday's close of 125.04. Turnover was a thin 13,899 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.275 percent as of 0628 GMT, down from Friday's close of 2.285 percent.
The cash bond market was quiet except for some hedge -selling ahead of Wednesday's auction and scattered selling of cash bonds by city banks, a brokerage house trader said.

"There was some selling of cash bonds in the morning by city banks, but they may have been selling cash bonds and buying JGB futures, and there was little negative impact on the market," the brokerage house trader said.
Dealers were also detected selling cash JGBs from the 190th to 197th issues on the upside, probably for hedging purposes ahead of Wednesday's 10-year JGB auction, the trader said.

Although the expected coupon rate of 2.5 percent for the new 10-year issue is unlikely to be attractive to everyone, the Finance Ministry's offer will probably be absorbed relatively smoothly, traders said.
